abrogate: to formally repeal or abolish a law or agreement
demur: to raise objections or show reluctance; n: an objection
recant: to formally withdraw a previous statement or belief
recidivism: a tendency to relapse into crime or bad behavior
remission: a temporary lessening of a disease's symptoms
renege: to go back on a promise or commitment
retrograde: moving backward or reverting to a worse state; v: to regress
disperse: to scatter or spread in different directions
diverge: to separate and go different ways; to differ
awry: off course; wrong from what was planned
careen: to rush headlong, lurching out of control
carom: to strike and rebound off a surface; n: a rebound
circumvent: to find a way around a rule or obstacle
gyrate: to move rapidly in a circle or spiral
labyrinth: a complicated maze or intricate network
meander: to follow a winding course; wander aimlessly
sidle: to move furtively, edging along at an angle
undulating: rising and falling in a wavelike pattern
vortex: a whirling mass of water or air, like a whirlpool
cacophony: a harsh, discordant mixture of sounds
clamor: a loud, insistent outcry or demand; v: to demand noisily
dissonance: lack of harmony or agreement; a clash
inexorable: impossible to stop or prevent; relentless
intractable: hard to manage, solve or control
intransigent: refusing to compromise or change views
obdurate: stubbornly refusing to change, unmoved by pleas
obstinate: stubbornly unwilling to change one's opinion
recalcitrant: stubbornly defiant of authority or control
refractory: stubbornly resistant to control or treatment
daunt: to intimidate or discourage through fear
pusillanimous: showing a contemptible lack of courage
recreant: cowardly or disloyal; n: a coward or traitor
trepidation: fearful apprehension about what may happen
dolor: sorrow or grief, especially deep mental anguish
elegiac: mournfully expressing sorrow for the dead or past
lament: to mourn or express regret about; n: an expression of grief
melancholy: deep, pensive sadness; adj: gloomy and sad
threnody: a song or poem of mourning for the dead
balk: to hesitate or refuse to proceed
dither: to be indecisive; n: a state of nervous indecision
oscillate: to swing back and forth between states
teeter: to wobble unsteadily, close to falling
vacillate: to alternate indecisively between opinions or choices
waver: to falter or become unsteady in resolve
digress: to stray from the main subject
expatiate: to speak or write at length on a subject
forage: to search widely for food or provisions; n: animal fodder
peregrination: a long journey or wandering, especially on foot
sojourn: a temporary stay; v: to stay briefly
libertine: one who lives without moral restraint, especially sexually
libidinous: having or showing strong sexual desire; lustful
reprobate: an unprincipled, immoral person; adj: morally unprincipled
